record.paper_title: 25 Open Questions About Vector Bundles and Their Moduli
record.original_question: Does the vanishing result analogous to Theorem 6.2, which compares the homology of the moduli space of rank-2 vector bundles with that of the irreducible component of the corresponding moduli stack for large c_2, extend from products of Pic-independent curves to every surface of general type?

evidence.quote: Question 24. Does a generalization of Thm. 6.2 holds for any surface of general type?
Theorem 6.2. [BGRS, Thm. 18] Assume c2 >> 0, and let Σ1, Σ2 be Pic-independent smooth projective curves. Then, for q < c2 we have Hq(Mc2(Σ1 × Σ2),Msc2(Σ1 × Σ2)) = 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a smooth complex projective surface of general type. For an integer $c_2$, let $M_{c_2}(S)$ denote the moduli space of Gieseker semistable rank-$2$ torsion-free sheaves on $S$ with fixed determinant and second Chern class $c_2$, and let $\mathcal{M}_{c_2}(S)$ denote the corresponding moduli stack; write $\mathcal{M}^s_{c_2}(S)$ for the open substack parametrizing stable (or "good") objects (so that the natural morphism $\mathcal{M}^s_{c_2}(S) \to M^s_{c_2}(S)$ realizes the stable locus). 

A pair of smooth projective curves $\Sigma_1, \Sigma_2$ is called Pic-independent when the Picard group of $\Sigma_1 \times \Sigma_2$ is generated by the pullbacks of line bundles from the two factors. It is known that for Pic-independent pairs $(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2)$ and for $c_2$ sufficiently large, one has the vanishing
$$H_q\!\left(M_{c_2}(\Sigma_1\times\Sigma_2),\, \mathcal{M}^s_{c_2}(\Sigma_1\times\Sigma_2)\right) \;=\; 0 \qquad \text{for all } q < c_2.$$

Question: Does the same vanishing statement hold for every smooth complex projective surface $S$ of general type? That is, is it true that for any such $S$ there exists $C(S)$ so that for all $c_2 \geq C(S)$,
$$H_q\!\left(M_{c_2}(S),\, \mathcal{M}^s_{c_2}(S)\right) = 0 \qquad \text{for all } q < c_2?$$
artifact.category_tag: Moduli of vector bundles on surfaces
artifact.status_search_result: The vanishing comparison theorem is established for products of Pic-independent curves via Kuranishi-space techniques, but no source found extends it to all surfaces of general type. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Kuranishi Map for Vector Bundles
status_evidence.snippet: Studies rank-2 bundles on products of Pic-independent smooth projective curves and the homology of Kuranishi spaces; results are stated for this restricted class of surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: The known vanishing result is proved for Pic-independent products; no extension to arbitrary surfaces of general type is provided.
